title: N-Dimensional Buffon Crossing Factor: Gamma Closed Form αₙ = Γ(n/2)/(√π·Γ((n+1)/2))
description: Solves the sphere-average recurrence for the n-dimensional Buffon crossing factor αₙ in closed form. The parent (BuffonsNeedleOQ02OQ01) defines αₙ recursively via α₂ = 2/π, α₃ = 1/2, α_{n+2} = (n/(n+1))·αₙ. This entry proves the single explicit Gamma-function formula αₙ = Γ(n/2)/(√π·Γ((n+1)/2)) for all n ≥ 2, eliminating the recursion. The proof shows the closed form obeys the same two base cases and the same recurrence — the latter being a one-line consequence of the Gamma functional equation Γ(x+1) = x·Γ(x) — and concludes equality by induction. Fully verified: 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext:
The n-dimensional Buffon crossing factor αₙ = E_{S^{n-1}}[|u₁|] is the expected absolute projection of a uniformly random unit vector onto a fixed axis — the quantity governing expected hyperplane crossings in the Cauchy–Crofton formula of integral geometry (Santaló, 1976). The parent formalization established the two-step recurrence α_{n+2} = (n/(n+1))·αₙ with base cases α₂ = 2/π and α₃ = 1/2, and listed the closed form αₙ = Γ(n/2)/(√π·Γ((n+1)/2)) as the open question its recurrence pointed toward.

That closed form is the sphere-average integral E_{S^{n-1}}[|u₁|] evaluated through the Beta/Gamma integral, and it is the exact discrete analogue of a Wallis product: the even/odd dichotomy (even dimensions rational multiples of 1/π, odd dimensions rational) is a direct shadow of Γ being factorial-valued at integers and √π-valued at half-integers. This entry closes the loop by proving the explicit formula and deriving every previously-computed value from it.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open question (from buffons-needle-oq-02-oq-01):** Solve the sphere-average recurrence for αₙ in closed form using Gamma-function values, replacing the per-dimension recurrence with a single explicit formula.

**Theorem.** For every dimension n ≥ 2, the recurrence-defined crossing factor equals
$$\alpha_n = \frac{\Gamma(n/2)}{\sqrt{\pi}\,\Gamma((n+1)/2)}.$$
overview.text: Solves the sphere-average recurrence for the n-dimensional Buffon crossing factor αₙ in closed form: αₙ = Γ(n/2)/(√π·Γ((n+1)/2)) for all n ≥ 2. The proof shows the Gamma closed form obeys the same base cases (α₂ = 2/π, α₃ = 1/2) and the same recurrence α_{n+2} = (n/(n+1))·αₙ — a one-line consequence of Γ(x+1) = x·Γ(x) — and concludes by induction. All previously computed values (α₄ = 4/(3π), α₅ = 3/8) are re-derived from the single formula.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Part I** defines gammaForm n = Γ(n/2)/(√π·Γ((n+1)/2)).

**Part II** evaluates the Gamma values needed at the base: Γ(3/2) = √π/2 and Γ(2) = 1, each a single application of the functional equation Γ(x+1) = x·Γ(x) together with Γ(1/2) = √π and Γ(1) = 1.

**Part III (key lemma gammaForm_rec)** proves the closed form satisfies the *same* recurrence gammaForm(k+2) = (k/(k+1))·gammaForm(k). Rewriting Γ((k+2)/2) = Γ(k/2 + 1) = (k/2)·Γ(k/2) and Γ((k+3)/2) = ((k+1)/2)·Γ((k+1)/2) collapses the whole identity to a single field_simp (Gamma positivity supplies the nonzero denominators).

**Part IV (main theorem)** proves crossingFactor n = gammaForm n by the identical two-step induction used for the recurrence: base cases n = 2, 3 by direct evaluation, and the (n+4) step because both sequences obey α_{k+2} = (k/(k+1))·α_k with the same base data.

**Parts V–VII** restate the formula cleanly, recover α₂,…,α₅ from it as sanity checks, and express the full n-dimensional Buffon expectation in closed form.
keyInsights: Uniqueness by recurrence: two sequences agreeing on two consecutive base values and obeying the same 2-step recurrence are identical — so proving the closed form is a *fixed point* of the recurrence suffices, no integral evaluation needed
The entire content of the closed form is the Gamma functional equation Γ(x+1) = x·Γ(x); once applied to both Gamma factors, the recurrence ratio k/(k+1) appears mechanically
Γ positivity on (0,∞) is exactly what licenses clearing the Gamma denominators, turning the recurrence identity into a one-line field_simp
Base cases hinge on the two canonical special values Γ(1/2) = √π and Γ(1) = 1; the even/odd split of αₙ traces back to these
The closed form subsumes all earlier per-dimension computations: α₄ = 4/(3π) and α₅ = 3/8 fall out as instances rather than separate calculations
prerequisites: Gamma function and its functional equation Γ(z+1) = zΓ(z)
Integral geometry (sphere averages, Cauchy–Crofton crossing factor)
Induction with a two-step (n ↦ n+2) recurrence

conclusion.summary: The open question of expressing the n-dimensional Buffon crossing factor without recursion is settled: αₙ = Γ(n/2)/(√π·Γ((n+1)/2)) for all n ≥ 2, fully verified with 0 sorries and 0 axioms. The proof is a uniqueness-by-recurrence argument — the Gamma closed form is shown to be a fixed point of the same two-step recurrence with the same base data — so it reduces entirely to the Gamma functional equation Γ(x+1) = x·Γ(x).
conclusion.implications:
**1. Recursion eliminated.** Every crossing factor is now a single evaluation of Γ, subsuming the parent's per-dimension computations (α₄, α₅) as instances.

**2. Structural clarity.** The even/odd rational-vs-π dichotomy is exhibited as a consequence of Γ at integers vs half-integers, via the base values Γ(1) = 1 and Γ(1/2) = √π.

**3. Method.** The proof illustrates uniqueness-by-recurrence: to identify a recursively-defined sequence with a candidate closed form it suffices to check finitely many base cases and that the closed form satisfies the same recurrence — no integral geometry is re-derived.

**4. Toward asymptotics.** With the exact Gamma form in hand, the sharp asymptotic αₙ ~ √(2/(πn)) (parent open question) becomes a Gamma-ratio estimate rather than a recurrence unrolling.
